tagline: Generate TypeScript interfaces from JSON with smart type inference
pageDescription: Free advanced JSON to TypeScript converter with smart type inference, optional properties and nested interface support. Convert API responses, JSON Schema, configuration objects and complex JSON structures to production-ready TypeScript interfaces. Features union types, enum detection, date parsing, custom naming conventions and readonly options. Includes Zod schema generation, validation code and mock data generators. Perfect for TypeScript developers building type-safe applications with external APIs. No signup, no registration — all processing in your browser.

instructions.title: How to use JSON to TypeScript

steps.title: Paste your JSON data
steps.description: Copy and paste JSON from an API response, configuration file, or any JSON source into the input area. The tool accepts objects, arrays, nested structures, and JSON Schema. Invalid JSON is highlighted with error messages.

steps.title: Configure TypeScript options
steps.description: Customize the output: choose between interfaces or types, set naming conventions (PascalCase, camelCase), enable optional properties with '?', add readonly modifiers, and configure enum detection for repeated string values.

steps.title: Review generated TypeScript
steps.description: The converter instantly generates TypeScript interfaces with smart type inference. Nested objects become separate named interfaces. Arrays are typed automatically. Union types and nullable fields are detected from your JSON data.

steps.title: Copy or generate Zod schema
steps.description: Copy the TypeScript interfaces to your clipboard, or switch to Zod schema output for runtime validation. The generated code is production-ready with proper imports, exports, and type annotations.

proTips: Paste a real API response for the most accurate type inference
Enable optional properties when JSON fields may be missing or null
Use enum detection for status fields like 'active' | 'inactive' | 'pending'
Generate Zod schemas when you need runtime validation, not just compile-time types
For large nested JSON, review generated interface names and rename if needed
Combine with readonly for configuration objects that shouldn't be mutated
troubleshooting: Invalid JSON error: Check for trailing commas, missing quotes, or unescaped characters
Empty output: Ensure your JSON contains at least one object or array
Types too broad (any[]): Provide sample data in arrays for better type inference
Missing nested interfaces: Verify nested objects are not empty {}
Browser compatibility: Use latest version of Chrome, Firefox, or Edge for best results
